title: Deferral Qualifying Payment Amount — Hardship Desk Figure Sheet
content:
**Amount.** On Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts, a deferral qualifying payment is the one-time partial payment a borrower makes on the contract when asking to defer an installment, made by the borrower from their own bank account. The deferral qualifying payment is the interest accrued on the principal balance from the last payment date to the payment date, at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis for each of those calendar days and rounded to the cent, plus the fees due on the contract. It posts as a partial payment applied to that accrued interest and then to those fees, and it never moves the next due date.

## Inputs and where they are read

| Input | Read from |
|---|---|
| Principal balance | the contract record |
| Contract APR | the contract record (the rate in effect) |
| Day-count basis | the tier's day-count basis: 365 days at every tier |
| Calendar days of interest | from the last payment date on the contract record to the payment date |
| Fees due | the contract record |

The interest is computed as one figure — the principal balance times the APR as a percentage, divided by the day-count basis, times the days — and rounded to the cent once.

## Worked figure (hypothetical contract)

Principal balance 9800.00, APR 15.59 percent, last payment date 2026-05-12, payment date 2026-06-03, fees due 40.00:

1. Days of interest: 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-03, 22 calendar days.
2. Accrued interest: 9800.00 times 15.59 percent, divided by 365, times 22, is 92.0878, rounded to 92.09.
3. Deferral qualifying payment: 92.09 plus 40.00, that is 132.09.
4. Split as entered: 92.09 to interest, 40.00 to fees, 0.00 to principal. The next due date does not move.

## Points of judgement

- A contract with no fees due has a deferral qualifying payment equal to the accrued interest alone.
- The payment is a partial payment, not a scheduled installment, whatever its size.
